title: Howling Fjord
body: The Howling Fjord is the southeastern doorway to Northrend, a land of deep sea inlets, pine forest and sheer bluffs, and the home of the vrykul, giants of whom there had been no sign for centuries and who have now woken in great numbers. The Alliance has come by sea to Valgarde and up the western cliffs to Westguard Keep, and the Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society have built Vengeance Landing to test a plague of their own, while the Scourge walks among the vrykul and iron dwarves seize the old dig sites.

title: Valgarde
body: Valgarde is the Alliance port on Daggercap Bay, built with bare hands, blood and tears, as its vice admiral puts it, one of only two safe harbors the Alliance holds in Northrend and the start of its main supply line. It has been on the defensive since the vrykul first struck it, and the Dragonflayer still hammer at its gate from Wyrmskull Village and the harpoon guns of Nifflevar on the bluffs.

parts.body: The seer saw the spirit world under the Lich King's sway, val'kyr standing watch over a terrible secret at Wyrmskull: an ancient vrykul couple over a newborn they took as a sign that they too were cursed.

title: Utgarde Keep
body: Utgarde Keep rises in the heart of the fjord, the stronghold from which the Dragonflayer vrykul make war. Its master is Ingvar the Plunderer, the champion these fearless giants esteem above all, and from its walls his raiders and proto-drake riders go out against Valgarde and Vengeance Landing alike. Above it, at the top of the crag, lies Utgarde Pinnacle, the higher hall of the vrykul.

title: Vengeance Landing
body: Vengeance Landing clings to the cliffs of the fjord's eastern shore, the Forsaken port in Northrend, and every soldier here has come for one reason: to see Arthas killed. Its high executor has served in many wars, always in other people's battles, but not this time. In its laboratory and at the plaguebringers' town of New Agamand to the west, the Royal Apothecary Society works on the plague it has brought north for the Scourge.

parts.body: Prince Keleseth of the San'layn came to the landing with an offer from Arthas: abandon Sylvanas's rebellion and command armies far greater. The high executor answered with his archers.
sources: Anselm npc_text 11796 (every Forsaken soldier here has come for one reason: Arthas must be killed)

parts.body: After what he called an eternity of failure, New Agamand's chief plaguebringer announced a strain to tear down the very fabric of life. He called it blight, and sent it to Venomspite in the Dragonblight.

title: Westguard Keep
body: Westguard Keep crowns the western cliffs of the fjord, commanded by the dwarf Captain Adams, a dwarf of action with a famous temper who has too few soldiers to hold the keep and garrison Fort Wildervar for the march into the Grizzly Hills. Pirates sank all its ships, and north of it the Explorers' League digs at Steel Gate, where most of its people went into Whisper Gulch and came back mad.

parts.body: The mad explorers rave that they have learned the truth and that it is coming, That Which Must Not Be Named, and the gulch's ore leaves a strange feeling in those who carry it.

title: Gjalerbron
body: Gjalerbron, its name spoken as if it began with Sh, is the great fortress of the vrykul in the north of the fjord, forbidden to the taunka. Cages line its paths, Scourge necrolords move among the vrykul, and beneath it, in the Waking Halls, rows of dormant vrykul stand waiting. At its northern end the chamber of the Winter's Terrace opens onto the slopes of Gjalerhorn.

parts.body: Queen Angerboda, wife of King Ymiron, drives a ritual there with the Scourge's help to wake her husband, demanding ever more sacrifices.
Angerboda was slain in the Winter's Terrace, but the Lich King himself came and carried the sleeping Ymiron off, which no one liked the sound of.

title: Kamagua
body: Kamagua is the village of the Kalu'ak tuskarr on the Isle of Spears, off the fjord's southwestern coast, under Elder Atuik. The tuskarr live mostly from the sea, but this season the catch is modest, and survivors of Iskaal, a village sacked by pirate slavers, keep pouring in. A great sea turtle carries travelers to the Dragonblight, and a gondola climbs from the isle to the bluffs, where the dead have risen at an old vrykul burial ground.

parts.body: Pirates had plundered the burial mounds. The relics were returned too late: the dead warned that the Kvaldir return out of the mist, and the Kalu'ak prepare for battle.
